# Sesh (quick session save)

Oscar closes terminals constantly. Each one holds a little useful residue that /bonsoir is too heavy to capture per-close. `/sesh` grabs just that residue in seconds and stashes it so nothing is lost, then he can close the tab guilt-free.

This is deliberately NOT /bonsoir. No dashboard update, no bagelHQ push, no god-mode doc, no status file rewrite. Fast in, fast out.

## What it does

1. **Read this session's context** and extract only what would be painful to lose:
   - Which project/repo this terminal was on (infer from cwd, git, what was discussed)
   - What was decided or built here (1-3 bullets, terse)
   - Open threads / what was mid-flight
   - THE single next action to resume this thread
   - Any uncommitted work worth noting (mention the repo; do not commit anything)
2. **Append a timestamped block** to the rolling stash file `~/.claude/projects/-Users-morkeeth/memory/sesh-stash.md` (create it if missing). Append, never overwrite. Format:

   ```
   ## <project> — <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM>
   - built/decided: …
   - open: …
   - next: …
   - uncommitted: <repo> has N dirty files (or "clean")
   ```
3. **Confirm in one line** and stop. Under 5 lines of output total.

## Rules

- Speed over completeness. If nothing meaningful happened, say "nothing worth stashing" and skip the write.
- Never commit, push, or touch the dashboard/bagel. That is /bonsoir's job.
- One block per close. Do not rewrite earlier blocks.
- Terminal-native, no artifact.

## The loop it closes

`/sesh` is append-only capture across the day. `/bonjour` READS `sesh-stash.md` and surfaces unresolved next-actions. `/bonsoir` CONSOLIDATES the day's stashes into the status file + Tomorrow's Objectives, then CLEARS `sesh-stash.md` so stashes never rot (doc-lifecycle rule 1: close the loop at write time).

## Links
Fast cousin of `/bonsoir`; feeds `/bonjour`. Discipline: context-capture / `context_anxiety` (evacuate thinking, never lose it), `parallel_sessions` (one terminal per project). Related: [[feedback-teach-tips-in-output]].

BENCHMARK's 93% is meaningless: measured on a static set, not live drafts. **The evaluator is the broken half, not the drafts.**
6	- built/decided: gold set 14 -> 44 labels. 21 bulk kills flagged in-note as "not individually reviewed" so they read as weaker signal. Consolidation done: project_x_engine + project_megafon_v2 + project_content_plan -> archive/, one content-engine memory (megafon was rot: pointed at a path the Next.js app has held since Jul 12, and its `name:` collided with project_taste_machine).
7	- built/decided: scout guards after it destroyed the corpus (361 tweets -> 0 on a 402): refuses to write an empty pool (exit 1), and refuses to re-scout inside 6h when a good cache exists. Corpus restored, 466 tweets. Jul 17 cost only ~9 requests; Jul 15's 208-request rebuild ate the month.
8	- open: Jul 17 rules recorded as HYPOTHESES (n=1 each, H1-H7, scoped to replies, in voice.md). Oscar: "these are hypothesis for now, we'll make a new list next time." Length rule downgraded from refusal to warning — he questioned it ("thats not a kill itself") and it was silently dropping drafts.
9	- open: 3 drafts held pending, he called them good but not sent: 0f10 @lennysan, 8806 @alexalbert__ (his artisanal-20% angle), bac2 @mem0ai. He is NOT ready to send anything yet; approved = queued, nothing posts (silent mode + shadow ban).
10	- open: wanted, not built — quote-tweets and image posts. The engine only knows replies; neither gate nor schema knows they exist.
11	- open: yield is ~2-3 draftable topics/day, not 10. From 466 fresh tweets only 8 were human+respected+<24h, and 2 cleared his topic gate. "10/day" needs a wider pool, not a lower bar. Also: dedup only catches exact prefixes, so one farm repost ("Google just dropped a 1-hour course") took 10 of the top 16 slots.
12	- next: **fix the gate to see what he actually judges** (topic, person, fun-or-smart) — worth more than another 10 drafts. Then: H3 @steipete veto belongs in the `people` table, not prose.
13	- next (Oscar only): 🔴 Supabase has NO access control — every table RLS-enabled + `app_all USING (true)` for anon; probed: 7 tables returned data, candidates took INSERT 201 + DELETE 204. Fix committed NOT applied (`supabase/migrations/20260717_lock_rls.sql` + `scripts/probe-anon.sh`): needs his **service_role key from the dashboard**, and the app authenticates AS anon so applying it first kills the app. **Gates publishing the repo public.**
14	- uncommitted: both clean. taste-machine + x-engine on `night-run-2026-07-13`, still NO git remote on either (that is why "unpushed" keeps recurring). x-engine stays private forever: voice.md is his voice corpus.
